cvEn:
Ezra Mantzur, son of Marcel and Yosef, was born on the 5th of Shevat 5713 (21 January 1953) in Holon. He studied at the "Shenkar" elementary school in Holon and afterward completed his studies at the "ORT" vocational high school in Holon. Ezra was a clever, diligent and hardworking student. According to his teachers, he excelled in the sciences and had a special talent for mathematics. By nature he was humble and modest, honest and kind-hearted, and he was always ready to help others. He set an example for his friends through his diligence, his dedication and the way he carried out the tasks entrusted to him. From his youth he loved art, and in his free time he liked to draw and to do various handicrafts. All his life he was devoted to his widowed mother and cared for his family.

Ezra was drafted into the IDF in early February 1972 and assigned to the Air Force. After basic training he took a course for Hawk missile technicians and was sent to serve at one of the Air Force bases in the south. In his unit Ezra was known as an excellent soldier, responsible and devoted to his role. His fellow unit members note that he was quiet and kept to himself, and he earned a reputation as a technician "you could rely on." Throughout his military service he tried not to worry his mother: he visited home often and was careful to call and write letters so that she would not suffer anxiety or concern. He never complained about difficulties, and he never spoke about his achievements. He was quiet and reserved.

When the Yom Kippur War broke out, he served as a Hawk missile technician in the Sharm el-Sheikh area. On the 10th of Tishrei 5734 (6 October 1973), Ezra was wounded in an air strike and killed. He was laid to rest in the cemetery in Holon. He is survived by his mother and a brother. After his death he was promoted to Sergeant. In a letter of condolence to the bereaved family, his commander wrote: "Ezra was beloved by his friends and his commanders, and his death is a great loss to all of us. I knew him well, and I know that all his thoughts were for the good of the IDF and for the good of his family. He always combined the good of both. I firmly believe that he was a good son, just as he was a good soldier."
